correctness.rationale: For independent u₁,u₂,u₃, the dual restriction ξ↦(−⟨ξ,u_i⟩) is onto, with p^(d−3) lifts per triple. After removing the common nonzero scalar and translation character, the four summands are unit complex numbers. If their sum is zero, the third elementary symmetric sum is the product times the conjugate of the first, so the monic root polynomial is even and the four numbers pair oppositely, including multiplicities. A pair requires a ratio in −μ_p; two disjoint pairs give two independent affine equations in the anchored three coordinates. Three matchings cannot be feasible: two −μ_p ratios along a length-two path force the third ratio into μ_p, disjoint from −μ_p. Two matchings give an alternating four-cycle; fixing the phase at site zero determines every other actual summand and feasibility puts it in its required coset. The two local lines have different directions and meet at one point. This gives all counts and the lifted subspace dimensions. The three listed witnesses give zero, one or two feasible matchings; in the two-matching case the four coefficient cosets are two copies of one coset and two of its negative, giving the equivalence classification. Inspected the frozen exact Gaussian-integer checker (artifacts/verify.py) without executing it; its finite set has 5271 planned checks. In the independently written `python3 /workspace/replay/check_assignments.py 4`, reduction at primes 41,29,89 and evaluation at every primitive p-th root and both signs of the square root of −1 makes an exact test for these bounded coefficient sums. At p=5,7,11 the 64 normalized quarter-turn phase choices give local spectra {0,5,9}, {0,7,13}, {0,11,21}; the witness zero lines and intersections agree. This does not test arbitrary phases; the proof does.

evidence: Let U=bμ_p, V=cμ_p, T=d/(bc)μ_p. The three prior branches in the product U×V×T are A: η=1,Z=−1; B: η=1,W=−1; C: W=−Z,η=Z^(−2). A and B are each empty or a size-p line in exponent coordinates. C is empty unless V=−U and T={z^(−2):z∈U}, in which case its graph is also a size-p line, since p is odd and all its exponent constraints are affine-linear.

A and B together give U=V=−μ_p, incompatible with C. If A and B exist they meet at (−1,−1,1); if A and C exist they meet at (−1,1,1); if B and C exist they meet at (1,−1,1). Directions are distinct. All three counts already result from T=μ_p with U=V=μ_p, U=−μ_p and V=iμ_p, or U=V=−μ_p, respectively. The condition for two lines forces two coefficient cosets of each opposite type, up to permutation and common normalization.

evidence: Normalize α₀=1 and write b,c,d for the other phases. In the rank-three local cube replace t₃ by s=t₃−t₁−t₂. Then Z=bω^t₁, W=cω^t₂, η=d/(bc)·ω^s range independently over three cosets and the polynomial is 1+Z+W+ηZW, precisely the earlier rectangle proof's normalized torus polynomial.

The rectangle proof states that at η=1 the zeros have Z=−1 or W=−1, and for η≠1 the torus zeros obey W=−Z and ηZ²=1, giving both roots. The latter relation at η=1 gives (−1,1),(1,−1), already included. The flat-parabola proof uses the same even-root-polynomial lemma, two opposite-term equations per matching, and the same μ_p versus −μ_p exclusion.
